7.4 MAGNITUDE QUAKE STRIKES PHILIPPINES, TSUNAMI ALERT ISSUED

A 7.4 magnitude earthquake hit off the Philippines’ east coast on October 10, prompting a PTWC warning for 1-meter waves within 300 km. The tremor follows September’s deadly Cebu quake, reaffirming the nation’s seismic exposure on the Pacific Ring of Fire. Evacuations are underway in Mindanao and Bacolod as aftershocks persist and authorities monitor coastal risks.

#PhilippinesEarthquake #TsunamiAlert

#SciFeature 𝗧𝗦𝗨𝗡𝗔𝗠𝗜 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗔𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦 𝗜𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗣𝗛𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗣𝗣𝗜𝗡𝗘𝗦 🌊

Kasabay ng napakalakas na Magnitude 7.6 na #linog (#lindol) sa silangan ng Davao Region ang banta ng mapaminsalang tsunami. Ating balikan ang kaalaman patungkol sa mga uri ng tsunami na posibleng maranasan ng ating baybayin at ilang mga lindol sa kasaysayan na nagdulot ng tsunami.

Ang mga tsunami ay kadalasang mga mapaminsalang mga alon na dulot ng mga malalakas na lindol, pagputok ng bulkan, o pagguho ng lupa sa ilalim ng karagatan. Dahil sa bilis at kadalasang umaangat na taas nito pagdating sa baybayin, ang mga tsunami ay karaniwang nagdudulot ng pinsala sa mga komunidad. 

Dahil ang Pilipinas ay pinalilibutan ng mga aktibong fault at trench at bukas rin sa malalaking karagatan, tulad ng sa Pasipiko, hindi maikakaila ang banta ng tsunami sa bansa. Ayon sa Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS), may tatlong pangunahing uri ng banta ng tsunami na maaaring maranasan sa mga baybayin ng Pilipinas: 

[𝟭] 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗛-𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗟𝗢𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗧 𝗧𝗦𝗨𝗡𝗔𝗠𝗜

Ang mga baybayin sa hilaga at silangang bahagi ng Pilipinas ang pinakaexposed sa ganitong banta ng tsunami, lalo pa at sila ay nakaharap sa Pacific Ocean. Sila ay maaaring maapektuhan ng tsunami mula sa malapit o malayong mga lindol na kadalasang dulot ng paggalaw ng mga trench. 

Halimbawa: Mapaminsalang tsunami sa silangang bahagi ng bansa mula sa 1960 Valdivia Earthquake sa South America

[𝟮] 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗛-𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗟𝗢𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗧𝗦𝗨𝗡𝗔𝗠𝗜

Ang mga baybayin sa kanlurang bahagi ng bansa ang kadalasang pinakaexposed sa ganitong banta ng tsunami dahil sa mga malalapit trench na nakalatag sa West Philippine Sea, Sulu Sea, at Celebes Sea. Ang mga tsunami mula sa malalapit na trench ay maaaring maging lubhang mapanganib dahil kadalasang ilang minuto lamang ang pagitan ng malakas na lindol at pagdating ng mapaminsalang tsunami. 

Halimbawa: Tsunami na dulot ng napakalakas na 1976 Moro Gulf Earthquake na gumulat at kumitil sa buhay ng higit sa 5,000 katao sa Mindanao

[𝟯] 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗧𝗢 𝗢𝗙𝗙𝗦𝗛𝗢𝗥𝗘 𝗙𝗔𝗨𝗟𝗧 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗦𝗨𝗕𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗡𝗘 𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗦𝗟𝗜𝗗𝗘 𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗦𝗨𝗡𝗔𝗠𝗜

Hindi man sila nakaharap sa malalaking karagatan, ang mga baybayin sa loob na bahagi ng ating kapuluan ay posible pa ring makaranas ng mga tsunami dulot ng mga paggalawa ng malapit na fault sa ilalim ng dagat o kaya mga pagguho ng lupa na maaaring tumulak ng maraming tubig. 

Halimbawa: Tsunami na dulot ng paggalaw ng Aglubang River Fault sa hilagang ng Mindoro island noong November 1994. 

Sa kasalukuyan, wala pa talaga tayong kakayanan upang pigilan ang mga mapaminsalang tsunami, pero maaari naman nating ihanda ang mga komunidad mula rito. Ang patuloy na pag-aaral sa mga natural hazard na ito at paghahanda ng mga mamamayan ay susi upang mas maraming mailigtas na buhay at mga ari-arian. #tsunami #EarthquakePH #lindol

Nagcourtesy visit si Highway Patrol Group (HPG) Acting Director Police Colonel Hansel Marantan at iba pang miyembro ng HPG sa head office ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) sa Pasig City.

Sa courtesy meeting, ibinahagi ng MMDA sa HPG ang mga pangunahing mandato ng ahensiya; Flood Control and Sewerage Management, Urban Renewal, Zoning and Land Use Planning and Shelter Services, Health and Sanitation, Urban Protection and Pollution Control, Public Safety, Development Planning, Solid Waste Disposal and Management, at Transport and Traffic Management.

Pinagusapan din ang mga ginagawang pagtugon ng ahensiya sa traffic management para sa kaayusan ng kalsada at kaligtasan ng publiko sa buong Kalakhang Maynila.

Personal din na pinakita ni Chairman Artes ang MMDA Communications and Command Center, ang ipinagmamalaking state-of-the-art facility ng ahensiya na nagsisilbing operations, data center, at center point area ng mga opisyal. Gamit ang mga CCTVS, dito isinasagawa ang monitoring sa lagay ng mga kalsada, pagbaha, at weather updates sa Metro Manila.

Ayon sa mga opisyal ng dalawang ahensiya, patuloy lang ang koordinasyon at pagtutulungan para sa kaligtasan ng publiko sa mga lansangan ng National Capital Region.

#mmda #mmdaatyourservice

Apolaki Caldera: Hidden Supervolcano Beneath Philippine SeasEast of Luzon in the Philippine Rise (formerly Benham Rise) lies the Apolaki Caldera, Earth's largest at 150 km diameter, surpassing Yellowstone and Toba. Formed by massive eruptions millions of years ago, it reshaped the seafloor. Named after the Filipino god of sun and war, this dormant feature highlights the Philippines' volatile Ring of Fire geology and was discovered in 2019 by geophysicist Jenny Anne Barretto's team using bathymetric mapping.

data.raw_text:
❗️⚠️🇵🇭 - A 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck offshore in the southern Philippines on October 10, 2025, at a depth of 10 km (6 miles) off Manay town in Davao Oriental province, Mindanao region. 

The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) warned of potential damage and aftershocks, urging coastal residents in central and southern areas to evacuate to higher ground or inland due to expected tsunami waves over 1 meter above normal tides.

Tsunami warnings covered multiple areas: up to 50 cm waves in Indonesia's northern Sulawesi and Papua; hazardous waves possible within 300 km (186 miles) of the epicenter per the U.S. Tsunami Warning System; and 1- to 3-meter waves in the Philippines, plus up to 1-meter waves in parts of Indonesia and Palau, according to the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center.

Davao Oriental Governor Edwin Jubahib reported resident panic and damage to some buildings, calling the quake very strong; local authorities were unreachable.

This followed the Philippines' deadliest quake in over a decade—a 6.9-magnitude offshore event near Cebu two weeks prior that killed 72 people. 

Situated on the Pacific Ring of Fire, the country sees over 800 earthquakes yearly. The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre rated it 7.4 magnitude at 58 km (36 miles) depth.

We must align with nature’s power, not pretend we’re above it.

Prayers and aid to everyone affected. 🙏

PRO7 HONORS EARTHQUAKE RESPONDERS IN HEROES’ WELCOME CEREMONY

The Police Regional Office (PRO) 7, under the leadership of Regional Director PBGEN Redrico A Maranan, hosted a Heroes’ Welcome Ceremony today, October 8, 2025, at the Cebu Police Provincial Office, Camp Arcadio Maxilom, Sudlon, Lahug, Cebu City, to honor and commend the gallant personnel deployed to the northern part of Cebu following the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck the province last week.

The ceremony celebrated the return of the PNP personnel who served as Search, Rescue, and Retrieval (SRR) teams, now recalled to their respective units to resume their duties in crime prevention, solution, and public safety. Despite their return, relief and rehabilitation efforts continue in the northern towns, with sufficient personnel still deployed to sustain assistance and recovery operations.

In his message, PBGEN Maranan expressed profound gratitude to the men and women of PRO7 for their bravery, sacrifice, and unwavering commitment during the critical period of disaster response.

He also extended his appreciation to the Regional Staff for their effective coordination and management that contributed to PRO7’s successful operations during the crisis, emphasizing that the region’s accomplishment lies in being on the road to normalcy and recovery.

The Regional Director further recalled the visit of President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr. to the province, highlighting the President’s commendation for Cebu’s quick and organized disaster response.

“As the President himself said, ‘Napakabilis nang responde ng Probinsya ng Cebu', and for that, I take my hat off and give my snappiest salute to Governor Pamela Baricuatro for orchestrating a very effective, responsive, and efficient disaster response,” PBGEN Maranan stated.

PBGEN Maranan also acknowledged the collective efforts of the Bureau of Fire Protection, Philippine Coast Guard, Armed Forces of the Philippines, other regional offices, and various government sectors for their solidarity and assistance in the ongoing disaster response and relief operations.

A highlight of the event was the presentation of awards to the Cebu Police Provincial Office (CPPO) key officers and contingents led by PCOL Abubakar U Mangelen Jr., Provincial Director, together with representatives from the different units of the deployed contingents.

They were conferred with the Medalya ng Pagtulong sa Nasalanta (PNP Disaster Relief and Rehabilitation Medal) for their active and exemplary performance in conducting inspections, close monitoring of affected areas, supervising personnel deployment, and providing vital support in clearing, search, retrieval, rescue, and relief operations in coordination with local government units and the Incident Command Post of Bogo City.

The Heroes’ Welcome Ceremony served not only as a tribute to the courage and compassion of the PNP personnel but also as a reaffirmation of PRO7’s steadfast commitment to public service, resilience, and unity in times of adversity.

“Together, we will continue to rise and rebuild, because in the heart of every disaster, the Filipino spirit always prevails,” PBGEN Maranan concluded.

-Too many traffic lights 
-People look different
